mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive forward returns in the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 8.5% over a one-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers a flight to safety and reduces equity risk appetite, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 8.5%, or the signal fails to generate a negative return in 70% of triggered cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a multivariate regression.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 94.0 for two consecutive months signals a contraction in real output, which increases recession risk and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 94.0, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) combined with rising housing starts (HOUST) signals strong aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint rise in RSAFS and HOUST fails to produce positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term is not significant (p > 0.05) in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 220.0 for two consecutive months indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 220.0, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200k in a single month, combined with a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market that may force the Fed to raise rates, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS > 200.0 and UNRATE < 8.9 fails to predict negative 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term is not significant (p > 0.05) in a multivariate model.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, which reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 shows a two-quarter decline, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
